captions.text: But superior technology is entirely irrelevant
if it terrifies the user.
That is the harsh, unyielding truth of the creative
curve. Being too early is indistinguishable
from being wrong. Too early is wrong.
If your audience's avoidance reflex overwhelms their approach
reflex, they will back away.
It doesn't matter how elegant your code is or
how profound your writing is.
If they feel unsafe, they leave.
So to hit that sweet spot, you have to
consciously engineer the collision.
And Ganet breaks down how the most successful creators
do this into four repeatable habits.
And the first habit, the absolute baseline is consumption,
which looks very different from how we typically consume
media. Let's set the scene to show what this
looks like in practice.
